notation_and_syntax.notes: Cursor reasoning applies to the stated chained-unit design, not arbitrary open-addressed slots.

evidence: Recomputed keys 0 and 4 from old bucket zero at capacity four to new buckets zero and four at capacity eight.
Confirmed after one step cursor=1, old remaining=1, and migrated bucket zero empty.
Confirmed key 8 inserts new, key 1 transfers from old to new on update, key 5 inserts new, completion retires old, and deleting key 4 leaves 0,1,5,8 with size four.
Checked capacity examples: key 5 maps 1 modulo 4 and 5 modulo 8; 90 keys across two 100-cell arrays differs under stated denominators.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Finite bucket counts do not establish bounded time for arbitrary chain length or payload cost.

evidence: Verified union exact-once invariant: new-valid entries plus old-valid entries at buckets >=cursor equal the logical map.
Verified bucket migration recomputes new reduction, empties old ownership, and advances cursor only after complete transfer.
Verified transfer-on-update prevents stale old values/duplicates and completion follows from cursor reaching old capacity.
Reviewed stop-the-world rebuild as a bijection with source retention through destination publication.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Amortized total work is not used as a proof of per-operation tail latency.

evidence: Checked all current entries match new capacity and all old entries match old capacity.
Checked old buckets below cursor are empty, keys are unique across generations, and combined physical count equals logical size.
Checked lookup, put/update transfer, delete, migrate, completion, and retirement preserve the finite map invariant.

Reviewed new insert, new update, old transfer-on-update, delete authority, whole-bucket migration, cursor advance, and exact size behavior.
Reviewed stop-the-world publication, incremental progress/debt, iterator semantics, nested-trigger policy, and deferred reclamation obligations.
proof_review.notes: Partial-unit, open-addressed, cooperative concurrent, and directory-split schemes retain architecture-specific proof obligations.

evidence: Redis details are scoped to current chaining source; Go bounded growth to current capped-directory tables; OpenJDK to its concurrent bin transfer; Abseil to its whole-table layout.
Amortized, latency, memory, progress, and security claims state separate evidence requirements.
ISO C++ and Rust API observations do not imply a physical migration algorithm.

pedagogical_review.notes: Builds from rebuild as representation transformation to a precise mixed-state authority model, contrasts four current architectures, includes a reproduced migration trace, twelve causal misconceptions, ten examples, and five progressive exercises with complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, source, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Redis/Go/OpenJDK/Abseil/runtime maintainer, security, performance, reliability, operations, architecture, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and finite trace prove neither generic exception/lifetime safety, bounded latency for arbitrary migration units, progress under arbitrary workloads/failures, production memory/cache superiority, HashDoS immunity, stable order/references beyond a named API, concurrent linearizability, safe reclamation, benchmark superiority, certification, nor deployment fitness.
